source.title: Localizing Persona Representations in LLMs
source.authors: C. Cintas; M. Rateike; Erik Miehling; Elizabeth Daly; Skyler Speakman

record.file_problem: None apparent; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures localized activation subsets and their overlap in LLM representations, a different method from toy-model superposition experiments.
record.gate_note: The study reports PCA-based layer separation and Deep Scan activation-localization results. The relevant findings for the claim versions are the measured overlaps and unique subsets of salient activation coordinates in Llama3's last layer. The paper does not test toy-model capacity pressure, sparse-feature SAE recovery, causal effects of the activations, or feature dimensionality.
record.test_reason: The study does not test superposition or any of its versions. It uses Deep Scan, an anomaly-scan method, to pick salient last-token residual-stream coordinates in Llama3-8B-Instruct's last layer for each persona, then counts how these coordinate sets overlap. The authors call the overlap 'polysemanticity' and cite Scherlis et al., but this is a related, different construct. The units are residual-stream coordinates, which have no privileged basis, not neurons. The sets are chosen by a detection score, not as features. No chance-overlap baseline is given, although each set covers roughly 1,100–2,700 of 4,096 coordinates (Tab. 4, 8). There is no SAE, no toy model, no capacity manipulation and no test of feature dimensionality. The overlap counts therefore cannot show whether features are superposed, spread across neurons, or recoverable by a dictionary.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors also find that the later-layer separation holds across Llama3, Granite and Mistral. They interpret the shared ethics activations as polysemy or polysemanticity, and political views as more distinctly localized. They state the methods are correlational and leave causal editing to future work.
record.recipe_differences: Uses PCA and clustering metrics for layer-wise separation and Deep Scan for salient activation localization and overlap; it does not construct toy networks, vary feature sparsity or importance, or test SAE dictionaries.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported activation overlap and uniqueness vary by persona topic. The study's layer-wise separation analysis also reports strongest separation in later layers, with some metrics favoring earlier layers or other models for some personas.

fits_no_version.finding: In Llama3-8B-Instruct's last layer, Deep Scan-salient residual coordinates overlap across personas within a topic. 17.55% are shared across all ethics personas, 9.42% across politics and 7.62% across personality. Across topics, overlap is between 0 and ~12%. No chance baseline is given.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Concept-salient coordinate subsets of LLM residual streams overlap across related concepts, a basis-dependent 'polysemantic overlap' distinct from neuron superposition.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the Eighth AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society (AIES2025)
record.problems: Localization and overlap results are presented only for Llama3's last layer; no causal intervention tests whether the identified activations generate persona behavior. The authors note that the findings depend on a selected, LLM-generated English dataset, primarily reflect WEIRD perspectives and U.S.-centered politics, and may not generalize. The study does not test SAE recovery.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant results omitted. PCA layer-separation results and Deep Scan validation scores for detecting matching-behavior labels were not recorded as rows because they do not directly measure the claim version's feature-overlap or dictionary-feature object.

untested.parts: All: no toy models, sparsity sweep or feature geometry.
All: no capacity manipulation or feature-importance analysis.
All: the study does not examine why units are polysemantic.
All: no SAE or dictionary, no neuron-level analysis (residual coordinates only), and no test of whether features are distributed beyond basis-free selection sets.
All: feature dimensionality is not examined.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V4 'supports' and 'limits_scope' labels are removed. Overlap among sets of selected residual-stream coordinates is not evidence of superposition. The residual basis is not privileged, and the set sizes (|OS*| roughly 1,167–2,692 of 4,096, Tab. 4 and 8) imply sizeable overlap by chance, with no null reported. R14 'CONSC' is likely CONSE. The PCA layer-separation and Deep Scan precision/recall results are rightly excluded.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, feature sparsity and importance, capacity pressure, and nearly orthogonal overlapping feature directions.
Whether polysemanticity results from limited capacity or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise through mechanisms other than capacity pressure, or whether polysemanticity alone evidences superposition.

The study localizes persona-related activation coordinates, but does not use SAEs, establish that features are complete or recoverable dictionary features, or directly show that a single feature is spread across many neurons.
SAE features and whether dictionary features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
Whether the represented features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional features.

rows.subject: Llama3-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Measured intersections of Deep Scan salient activation subsets for ethical personas in the last layer.

conditions.value: salient activation subsets across ethical personas

rows.measure: Activations shared across all ethical personas
rows.note: The authors interpret the substantial shared activation subset as polysemantic overlap among ethical representations.
rows.check: Overlap of Deep Scan-selected residual-stream coordinates across ethics personas. These are not neurons or dictionary features, and no chance baseline is given for sets of over 1,000 coordinates out of 4,096. The authors' 'polysemanticity' reading is an interpretation, not a V4 measurement.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The measured salient sets include shared and persona- or topic-specific activation coordinates, with overlap varying across topics (R1-R6, R8-R16).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Comparisons across topic-level activation sets in Llama3-8B-Instruct
reader_labels.reason: Overlap differs materially by topic, including no Ethics–Personality intersection but roughly 12% Politics–Personality overlap; the findings are from one model's last layer and do not establish SAE feature recovery (R7-R10).
